claim: Model-made conjectures are mostly false, duplicate or trivial, so a cheap falsification and filtering funnel must dominate the loop. Chuharski: of 420 unique conjectures only 40 (9.5%) survived counterexample search; LeanConjecturer: 3,776 of 12,289 (30.7%; 34.5% of syntactically valid) not aesop-provable.
agent_test: Same token budget: generate N candidate claims, then (a) accept all vs (b) code-run falsifier plus novelty/triviality filter; compare share of kept claims that survive an independent check.

claim: Survival rate is a poor quality score: the model with most surviving conjectures (GPT-4, 26.6%) mostly wrote easy size statements. Pair survival with a nontriviality/sharpening check (Graffiti Dalmatian rule).
agent_test: Score kept conjectures by survival alone vs survival plus sharpening over the existing set; rate usefulness by blind check.

claim: Systems that find new mathematics pair a generator with an automated checker (Lean, numeric evaluator, counterexample code, verifier agents); where the checker can be gamed it is gamed (AlphaEvolve leaky verifier).
agent_test: Run the same task with a code checker vs model self-check at equal tokens; add a hold-out check and count gamed passes.

claim: A learnability or hold-out probe plus a targeted counterexample from an unsampled region and an added variable reproduces the Lakatos lemma-incorporation move (Davies: slope bound refuted by braid knots, injectivity radius added; slope-only linear model also 78%). A failed probe is weak evidence and must not drop a conjecture.
agent_test: Seeded items with hidden-variable conjectures; compare refine-after-counterexample vs resample at equal tokens on final correctness.

claim: Lakatos's three counterexample types (global-not-local, local-not-global, both) give a typed, code-checkable rule for what to change: the proof step, the claim, or both. No study varies this move directly on LLMs. Gap search: no LLM study compares typed against untyped counterexample reaction (d18); CRAFT (d03) is the nearest feedback-and-repair loop.
agent_test: Prompt arm with typed reaction vs untyped 'fix it' on seeded false-lemma items; token-matched.

claim: Decomposing into ordered subproblems (Least-to-Most) is the best-supported Polya-type heuristic in LLM tests; the plan-then-execute prompt gives only a few points on weak models (PS+ 76.7 vs CoT 70.4 average, GSM8K 59.3 vs 56.4).
agent_test: Decompose vs plan-only vs plain at equal tokens on multi-step math; report per model, since gains shrink with model strength.

claim: Polya heuristics given as prompts have model- and task-dependent effects, sometimes negative (auxiliary elements in geometry: GPT -25%, Haiku +14%; blog, unreviewed). A bag of heuristics without a selector is weak (Schoenfeld, secondary source).
agent_test: Fixed heuristic list in prompt vs program-selected single heuristic per state vs none; token-matched; per problem type.

claim: Frontier models over-trust their proofs: LLM graders inflate proof scores by up to 20x, the best model proves false statements 29.0% of the time (BrokenMath), and models claim to have solved problems they did not.
agent_test: Self-grade vs rubric+reference grader vs code check on proofs with known flaws; measure inflation at equal tokens.

claim: Proof-writing is much weaker than answer-giving and than seen-problem performance: 2025 USAMO best 10.1/42 (24%) for Gemini-2.5-Pro, others 2.0 or less; IMO-Bench Grok 4 heavy 76.2% on USAMO 2025 but 11.1% on novel problems.
agent_test: Use novel problems only for scaffold evaluation; report the seen vs novel gap.

claim: Counterexample construction is harder than judging a statement false: CounterMATH strict example scores fall well below judgement F1; open 7B models 28-38 F1, best commercial 80.7 F1; 1,025-sample SFT helps a little. Gap search: a 2026 tuned model reaches 49.8% pass@1 on formal counterexample validation vs 25.4% for the best baseline (d01), so it is trainable but still hard.
agent_test: Ask for a counterexample object that code verifies vs a true/false label; compare accuracy at equal tokens.

claim: Self-made conjectures used as RL training data raise proof counts on the same topic (2,285 to 5,307 of 24,576) but problems solved barely move (47 to 50 of 192) and transfer to 14 held-out items shows no clear gain.
agent_test: Not testable without training; at inference, test whether stored own-conjecture lemmas help on later same-topic items.

claim: Having the model write a search program or generator, scored by code, beats asking for the final object; small-case pattern, then general formula, then proof, then formal check is a workable chain, but over-generalising small-case patterns is a known failure.
agent_test: Search-program arm vs direct-answer arm at equal tokens on scorable construction tasks; add a held-out larger-n check.

claim: Generator yield is very prompt- and context-sensitive (one Mathlib file: 1 conjecture without 'as many as possible', 412 with; Chuharski found prompt wording did not fix duplicates; showing all prior conjectures raises diversity).
agent_test: Measure unique-and-novel yield per 1k tokens under three context policies.

claim: Skeptic/verifier structure beats generator-only in small tests: homology rediscovery proven useful formulas 12.7% full vs 5.9% without skeptic vs 0% conjecturer only; research-level sprints localise gaps with dependency diagrams. All small-N or self-reported. Gap search: no replication outside the homology toy domain (d10, d11); the system is a small symbolic RL model, not an LLM.
agent_test: Single agent with explicit skeptic phase vs without at equal tokens on seeded false-lemma items.

claim: Skipping the conjecture step inflates formal-proof results: autoformalisation scores are overestimated when the answer or bound is given (ConjectureBench, abstract only). Gap search: opened the paper; ConJudge GPT-4.1 78.77 seen vs 26.70 unseen at pass@1 (d15).
agent_test: Evaluate with and without the answer given; report the gap for our agent.

claim: Open collaborative refinement (Polymath) works when small contributions are checkable; failures exist (Polymath5 not solved by the project itself).
agent_test: Multiplayer idea; not testable in a single agent.

claim: Repeated attempts keep the same wrong strategy (lack of creativity is a top failure class), so an impasse rule that forces a different operator is needed.
agent_test: After a failed attempt, force a different heuristic vs free retry at equal tokens; count distinct strategies and success.

claim: Polya's look-back phase is the least implemented; one fine-tune raises the look-back share of dialogue from 16.5% to 23.4% but no accuracy is measured.
agent_test: With vs without a code-triggered look-back step (re-check, generalise, find another proof) at equal tokens.

claim: A code-checked loop is gamed unless the checker is hard to exploit; in one AlphaEvolve problem the fix was to shrink the search space (bounded step functions) so the scorer was valid. Only anecdotes, no rates and no hold-out test.
agent_test: Run a claim-refinement loop with the checker alone vs checker plus a held-out second checker; count accepted claims that fail the hold-out.

claim: Separate prover and verifier contexts may cut self-confirmation: QED verifier accepted 17 of 214 candidates and experts accepted all 17 (0/17 false positives, upper bound about 18%). Self-reported, no single-context control.
agent_test: Same proofs, verifier with vs without the prover's reasoning in context; compare false accepts against expert labels.

claim: Whether a typed Lakatos reaction (change the claim, the step, or both) beats untyped retry at equal tokens is untested. Nearest evidence is feedback-and-repair (CRAFT, 78 to 94% on 50 claims, abstract only).
agent_test: Counterexample found: arm A retries freely, arm B must label the reaction (claim, step, definition) then act; equal tokens; score final survival under an independent check.

claim: A 2026 multi-agent scaffold with separate planner, prover and verifier produced 5 expert-confirmed original proofs from 18 open research projects (QED), and a sprint closed 4 of 10 problems with full validation (First Proof Sprint). Both self-reported with no equal-token no-scaffold arm, so the scaffold's own contribution is unknown.
agent_test: Run the same open items with a single long call at equal tokens and compare expert-confirmed results.
